tool.name: Concatenate MAF pieces
tool.description: : of one reference sequence, in coordinate order
tool.command: ## Galaxy flattens newlines in <command>, so the work is a POSIX sh script with its inputs as argv, ## never Cheetah, so the same script runs as a UDT. The pieces arrive as one comma-separated list. sh '$script' '$reference' '$output' '$pieces'

param.name: pieces
param.label: MAF pieces of one reference sequence
param.help: roast's outputs for the pieces of one reference sequence, in any order. The reference must be the top row of every block, and the pieces must not overlap.

param.name: reference
param.label: Reference name
param.help: As it prefixes the reference rows (cs10_NCBI_RefSeq_softmasked for cs10_NCBI_RefSeq_softmasked.NC_044376.1). Letters, digits and _ only.

has_text.text: the pieces cover more than one reference sequence: chr21 and chr22
the reference start goes backwards in piece 1

tool.help:
**What it does**
Joins the MAF pieces of **one** reference sequence (roast's outputs for the pieces of a split) into one MAF in reference coordinate order, as UCSC's multizNway builds do before ``mafAddIRows`` and ``mafToBigMaf``.
The pieces may arrive in any order. Each piece's position is read from its content: the reference row (the top row of each block, ``<reference>.<sequence>``) of its first block. Pieces with no blocks (a header only) are skipped. Every ``#`` line is removed (roast writes ``##maf`` and ``#`` lines mid-file); the output has one header, the first ``##maf version=1 scoring=...`` line of the first piece in coordinate order, then every block followed by one blank line, then ``##eof maf``.
The job fails, with the reason on stderr, if:
* a block's top row is not the reference; * the pieces cover more than one reference sequence, or one piece holds two; * two pieces overlap (one ends past the start of the next, in reference coordinates); * a reference start goes backwards inside a piece.
If no piece has blocks the output is a header and ``##eof maf`` and stdout says so: a reference sequence can have no alignment. stdout reports ``pieces: N (M with blocks)``.
